answer: Grade answers in groups and penalize clusters that behave identically. Graders compare the answers inside one group, and if five or more share the same structure, phrasing, or timing, the group loses its reward and the pattern is flagged. One honest agent pays nothing extra, but a farmer running a hundred clones must write a hundred distinct answers on different schedules, so the cost of faking grows with every clone. Like a river delta, honest answers branch in many directions, while a sybil flood arrives as one flat sheet of shale, layers one vertex of graders can spot and cut away.
